sn56.36:1.1: “Bhikkhus, suppose a man were to cut up whatever grass, sticks, branches, and foliage there is in this Jambudipa and collect them into a single heap.
sn56.36:1.3: he would impale the large creatures in the ocean on the large stakes, the middle-sized creatures on the middle-sized stakes, and the small creatures on the small stakes.
sn56.36:1.4: Still, bhikkhus, the gross creatures in the ocean would not be exhausted even after all the grass,
sn56.36:2.1: sticks, branches, and foliage in Jambudipa had been used up and exhausted.
sn56.36:2.2: The small creatures in the ocean that could not easily be impaled on stakes would be even more numerous than this.
sn56.36:2.4: Because of the minuteness of their bodies.
sn56.36:2.5: “So vast, bhikkhus, is the plane of misery.
sn56.36:2.6: The person who is accomplished in view, freed from that vast plane of misery, understands as it really is: ‘This is suffering.’… ‘This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering.’ “Therefore, bhikkhus, an exertion should be made to understand: ‘This is suffering.’… An exertion should be made to understand: ‘This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering.’”
